items.title: Sustainability of Public finances and vitality of private sector crucial for development
items.summary: Maputo, 02 Nov (AIM) – Mozambican Finance Minister Carla Louveira believes that sustainability of public finances and the vitality of the private sector are complementary and interdependent dimensions of the country’s development. “Mozambique recorded growth of 1.7 percent in the second quarter of 2026, accompanied by a reduction in inflation to around six percent between August and September. These indicators reflect signs of a gradual recovery in economic activity, despite the challenges that continue to constrain the resumption of productive capacity”, the minister said. Speaking at the sixth edition of the Business Breakfast, which was organised by the country’s Confederation of Business Associations (CTA), which brought together government representatives, businesspeople and financial institutions to discuss the challenges of economic policy and its role in stimulating economic activity, Louveira said that strengthened partnership between government and CTA is crucial.

items.title: ExxonMobil doubles stake in Mozambique’s Rovuma LNG project to 50% through Eni asset swap
items.summary: ExxonMobil has increased its stake in Mozambique’s planned Rovuma liquefied natural gas (LNG) project to 50% from 25%, following an asset swap with Eni. Under the deal, Eni gave up its share of the project in exchange for other properties in the region ExxonMobil continues to lead the development as operator. The deepwater project sits in the Rovuma Basin off Cabo Delgado province and is designed to produce 18.6 million tonnes of LNG per year. Total development costs are estimated at US$30 billion. The partners have recently committed US$1.1 billion to long lead subsea and equipment contracts, which keeps the schedule on track for a final investment decision (FID) by the end of 2026 and first commercial operations in 2031 The Area 4 consortium also includes China National Petroleum Corp. (CNPC), Korea Gas Corp.

items.title: For US Democrats, climate policy is now about energy bills
items.summary: Climate change has all but disappeared from Democrats' campaign pitches, replaced by promises to lower electricity bills. But what would the party actually do on climate if it wins control of Congress? President Donald Trump's administration has gutted US climate policy . Yet even as wildfires, record heat waves and flooding hit communities across the country, Democrats are keeping quiet about global warming on the midterm campaign trail Instead, candidates are packaging climate policy as an affordability issue, stressing how Americans are struggling to afford gas, groceries and to insure their homes against climate-fueled weather extremes Take Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico in Texas, who represents the party's best chance at winning the race in the Republican stronghold in nearly 40 years.

items.title: Major fire destroys large part of HCM Oncology Department
items.summary: Maputo, 02 Nov (AIM) – A major fire on Sunday destroyed a large part of the Oncology Department at Maputo Central Hospital (HCM), the country’s largest health facility, causing material damage but “it did not reach the bunker, which is the core area for radiotherapy services.” According to the health minister, Ussene Isse, speaking to reporters, radiotherapy is highly sensitive to high temperatures, which means that absence of visible damage “does not necessarily mean the equipment remains in working order.” The minister explained that a multisectoral team is currently on-site conducting an assessment to determine the extent of the damage. However, there were no fatalities or injuries resulting from the fire. All 22 patients admitted to the Oncology ward were evacuated in a timely manner, “thanks to the intervention of the various sectors involved in the emergency response.” “Of the 22 evacuated patients, 12 have been discharged, while the remaining 10 have been transferred to the Dermatology Department, where they continue to receive medical care and psychological support.

items.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.summary: Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff to pay for a sharp rise in its fuel costs which have surged following the US-Israel war with Iran The carrier said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and said it expects European airfares to increase to help cover the cost But it said that was unlikely to be enough and, among a number of measures, it is looking into "temporary pay freezes".

items.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
